about.title: Sonora Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls in Sonora happen in the same everyday places as anywhere else — a grocery aisle off Mono Way, a poorly lit stairwell near S Washington Street, an icy parking lot along Rt 49 during winter, or a cracked sidewalk near Sanguinetti Road. What separates a serious claim from a dead end is usually whether someone can show the property owner knew, or should have known, about the hazard and did nothing about it. That's why documenting the scene matters so much here: photos of the spill, ice, or broken step, names of witnesses, and a request for any surveillance footage before it gets erased. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise outcomes — we're a free service that connects you with an independent attorney familiar with how these Tuolumne County premises cases are built and pursued, working on contingency so there's no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Sonora Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California law generally requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before it caused harm. An attorney can help gather the evidence that speaks to that notice, from maintenance logs to prior complaints.

items.title: Evidence Disappears Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage at stores and businesses is often erased within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can make or break a claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Case
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you were partly responsible for the fall, though any recovery may be reduced by your share of fault.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Sonora?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a public building near downtown Sonora, that deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. It's best to have an attorney review the specifics as soon as possible.

items.question: What if I fell at a business but wasn't sure what caused it?
items.answer: That's common, and it's part of why prompt documentation matters. An independent attorney can help investigate the scene, request incident reports, and pursue store surveillance video that may show exactly what happened before it's deleted.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We're not a law firm ourselves — we simply help connect injured people in Sonora and Tuolumne County with independent legal help.
